It's concluded that only linear co-adding sequences with positive weights maintain the original PSF, whereas other sequences introduce distortions. An example involving Hubble Space Telescope images is presented to illustrate the effect of co-adding sequences on the point spread function and its implications for image analysis.

This study establishes a novel connection between the Gaussian free field and a dynamic version of the Dyson model, previously investigated in an academic paper (examining the convergence rate of Riemannian cubature methods on hypersurfaces in Euclidean space). We represent the Gaussian free field as a sum of independent components, one of which evolves over time according to the Dyson model, while the other remains static, allowing us to approximate the Riemannian cubature method using an ensemble of Dyson models. We analyze and provide bounds for the approximation's error in this representation method, revealing that it relates to the geometric features and curvature of the underlying hypersurface.

In this research, we address the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in multi-dimensional space with smooth periodic initial conditions and obtain analytical estimates of the solution's maximum norm, tied to the initial conditions' maximum norm.

The verification problem for quantum computation is crucial as it enables a client, holding minimal quantum resources, to delegate a computational task and receive accurate results from a server with quantum capabilities. Currently, the fastest known protocol for verifying classical computation in quantum form requires O(n^2) communication. This protocol has a fundamental limitation, as it cannot be basic client to perform faster than linear time on input. Surpassing this barrier with improvements beyond the current protocol is an essential goal for developing more efficient and scalable quantum computation verification protocols. This paper introduces a novel, probabilistic quantum algorithm for matrix multiplication that achieves a runtime of O(n^(1 + ε)) with ε being an arbitrary positive value. This algorithm utilizes quantum memory and processing power, including an ideal black-box database, to perform matrix multiplication more efficiently. This achievement paves the way for verifying classical computation in quantum form more effectively, as demonstrated by the development of a single-server verification protocol for NP problems in classical input and output, with a runtime of O(n log^2 n).

Generating synthetic cell shapes that accurately reflect biological realism is a fundamental challenge for developing and testing image analysis tools and image acquisition procedures in cell biology. Both existing methods for creating fake cell shapes either lack detailed features or are tied to particular imaging techniques. In response, this study proposes a novel approach using level sets of signed distance functions to create cell shapes. This method allows for the development of cell shapes with various filament lengths, radii, and cross-sections, as well as membranes that are either transparent or imaged from a side view. Additionally, the method includes the creation of synthetic images from these generated shapes, as well as false negative staining patterns, to facilitate the image-based analysis for cell segmentation. Furthermore, the study also creates artificial cell shape change videos, as well as movie frames, to simulate time-lapse imaging for training deep neural networks for cell segmentation. All related code and materials for the tool called CellCreator can be found on GitHub at https://github.com/medipix-it/CellCreator.

Researchers in neural perception, cognition, and robotics are revisiting basic assumptions about spatial understanding, suggesting more suitable alternatives to the widely used Cartesian system. These systems utilize point-based representations, such as POIs (Places of Interest), or grid-based and term-based representations, which are more similar to how humans perceive space. Instead of relying on Cartesian coordinates, these alternative systems utilize inherent characteristics of their representations, such as POIs or a given grid, to determine the significance and connectivity between spatial elements, forming a map of interconnected areas. Unlike continuous Cartesian representations, these discrete systems make it easier to distinguish between distinct areas. However, a major challenge with POI-based models is their dependency on external knowledge about which areas are significant. On the other hand, a method called intrinsic POI discovery can automatically identify meaningful spatial boundaries and their corresponding POIs, making it highly relevant to tasks like navigation. A key goal in neural navigation is to create a neural representation of the environment, similar to a cognitive map in humans, allowing an agent to navigate through unfamiliar areas. A major limitation of existing continuous Cartesian and term-based models is their inability to provide clear, discrete spatial representations, making it challenging to establish a direct link to brain-inspired models of navigation. A method called MapLinkSpace was developed to bridge this gap by combining a term-based map of the environment, built from depth images, with a neural network of interconnected spatial areas, similar to a cognitive map in the brain, enabling seamless navigation through unfamiliar areas.

To evaluate the efficiency of event-chain Monte Carlo algorithms for complex systems with strong repulsive forces, we apply our methods to models featuring both short-range and long-range Coulombic interactions in two and three dimensions. Our study reveals that our high-performance ECMC scheme significantly outperforms standard local Metropolis algorithms by a factor of 20 to 300, while also being comparable to other enhanced local reversible methods, enforcing-move algorithms, and cluster moves for systems experiencing long-range Coulombic forces.

This paper highlights the effectiveness of a convolutional recurrent neural network in solving sound event detection and localization tasks by utilizing a dataset of real-world soundscapes recorded at specific locations with known coordinates. For the problem at hand, we trained and evaluated the accuracy of a previously described system and demonstrated that spatial information can be represented as location-based feature maps for the purpose of sound classification, localization, and detection tasks.

Traditionally, wireless communication systems avoid parallel transmission due to interference. However, in practice, total orthogonality is impractical in various contexts. Therefore, parallel transmission is frequently employed in wireless power transfer and future systems. This increased use has made simultaneous transmission a vital area of research for the next generation of wireless systems. A new approach to signal design for parallel transmission is presented in this paper, aiming to minimize noise power given a specific sum of weighted transmitted energies. The solution involves an algorithm based on the power flow method and numerical results demonstrate its effectiveness and potential in various applications like wireless communications and power transfer.

Time-frequency analysis heavily relies on spectrograms, being a fundamental component of time-frequency methods. The average power spectrum, being a Gaussian analytic function, theoretically possesses infinite zero points, yet in practical applications, we encounter a limited number of zero points, influenced in part by the discretization process. We aim to elucidate the mechanism behind this phenomenon. Our investigation centers on a specific type of spectrogram known as the Wigner spectrogram, enabling us to establish a direct link between underlying physical properties and the formation of clusters near the zero points of the spectrogram. We verify this theory through both numerical simulations and real spectrogram data from W. S. Cowan's W. Stitt G. Cowan's high-quality recordings of his baritone voice.

We present a novel universal method for detecting stable chimera states in diverse types of phase oscillator networks, whether they are linear or feature complex nonlinearity. This method is based on a novel type of chimera state reduction technique. To illustrate its efficacy, it was applied to three distinct examples: the Kuramoto model with symmetric connections, the same model with random connections, and the jellium model with a specific type of interaction.

A novel module is presented, allowing researchers to model complex systems influenced by random forces impacting particle motion, a phenomenon anticipated to occur within environments like turbulent planetary disks and the remnants of planetesimal disks. This module streamlines the creation of synchronized noise with variable intensity and auto-correlation time for each particle, with low memory requirements, and is available at no cost through the REBOUNDx supplementary module suite.

Key aspects of quantum science include precise measurement and feedback mechanisms, 
essential for various quantum technology applications like error correction, 
quantum control, and measurement-based computation. Theoretical frameworks 
for measurement-based quantum information processing are well-established, 
yet experimental realization remains largely pending due to the intricacies 
associated with quantum state feedback. This study presents a practical 
implementation of quantum feedback through a combination of specific 
types of quantum operations and measurement-based computation principles, 
enabling a reliable form of quantum state feedback. A critical 
component involves context-independent application of anti-hermitian gates, 
facilitating feedback control that is independent of underlying quantum processes. 
This discovery is demonstrated via integration of a superconducting qubit and 
photon-detection technology, showcasing its utility in various 
applications, including quantum filtering.

In a long and narrow container with horizontal axis, $N$ disks are placed inside, with their centers constrained to a 2D plane. A system like this can represent various physical phenomena including atomic structures, traffic behavior, and granular substances. The outer boundaries of the container are connected to a jamming controller which modifies its dimensions to slowly decrease its length until the system reaches an unrelaxable, or jammed, state. Due to the presence of internal springs that counteract the compression, each jammed configuration can persist under small fluctuations of the controller's controls. The system explores a diverse set of jammed configurations characterized by specific arrangements of the disks within the channel. To understand these configurations better, a model was developed that generates an ensemble of jammed states based on two factors: the density of the disks and their available freedom to move within the channel. The distribution of these jammed states within this ensemble was found to be influenced by two variables: the overall density of the disks and their 'freedom' variable. The relative positions of the disks within individual jammed states were discovered to follow a random distribution, characterized by a geometric pattern, provided the overall density is below a 2D version of the close-packed density. The distribution's characteristics, however, are influenced by the specific arrangement of the disks. The positions' fluctuations within individual jammed states were found to increase with both the overall density and their 'freedom' variable. The study identified critical thresholds that mark

Research indicates that climate system interactions lead to two distinct types of El Ni\~{n}o phenomena: East Pacific and Central Pacific types, which exhibit different global effects on seasonal precipitation. This study reveals that East Pacific El Ni\~{n}o is associated with intensified rainfall and wind patterns across the Pacific, polar regions, and Europe, whereas Central Pacific El Ni\~{n}o leads to altered atmospheric circulation patterns with minimal impact on precision at high latitudes. This knowledge was applied to EastSuper-ENSO, a simplified model of El Ni\~{n}o with an extended spatial scale, demonstrating that increasing its size from Central to East Pacific sizes enhances its capacity to induce precipitation and 850hPa wind anomalies globally, even with minuscule sea surface temperature changes. This finding suggests that the propagation of heat from the Pacific to other global regions is influenced by the size of El Ni\~{n}o, providing a theoretical basis for the distinct global effects observed between the two El Ni\~{n}o types.

Research on massive black holes has primarily focused on those located in galaxies of the Milky Way, Andromeda, or those connected to the external galaxy, while little is known about these objects in smaller, darker galaxies. A new study aims to investigate massive black holes in smaller galaxy formations. The study utilizes sensitive detection methods to analyze data from nine such objects formed through a novel process. The findings reveal that these black holes can create distinct signs when they merge, providing evidence for their existence. The study also discovers a new, intrinsically bright type of black hole that can shine brightly, even at greater distances. The knowledge of these black holes may help scientists locate and track them, allowing for a better understanding of how they influence the evolution of smaller galaxy formations.

In systems with electronic flat bands, quantum properties such as superconductivity, magnetism, and topological order are frequently found.  Although theoretical models exist, experimental verification remains challenging due to the complexity of engineering such systems with a flat band.  This work presents the first experiment demonstrating a quantum Hall system with all electrons in the lowest Landau level (LLL) exhibiting a Laxian topological order with a flat second LLL.  A Laxian wavefunction is constructed by combining Chern simulator circuits with a flat band in the second LLL, resulting in highly entangled states that match the characteristics of a topological order.  This order is characterized by a set of Wilson loops that can be experimentally measured and control the interaction strength to observe many-body phenomena such as Laxian spin liquids and magnetic ordering phase transitions.  This research provides new insight into many-body quantum systems with topological order and offers experimental techniques to manipulate such systems to achieve various phases of matter.

Understanding how genetic variations impact trait development and disease is a primary objective of complex trait genetics. Researchers have developed a model, the SNP architecture model, to categorize SNPs based on their potential functional significance. This model predicts that certain areas rich in Informed SNPs, those associated with specific traits or diseases and overlapping with DNase-I hypersensitive sites, show enrichment for heritable regions and show negative linkage disequilibrium decays with increased distance from gene promoters. Conversely, Uninformed SNPs, those not associated with DNase-I hypersensitive sites, lack these patterns and show no such concentration in gene promoters. This concentration difference suggests that Uninformed SNPs, potentially more closely linked to gene regulation, could have an impact. However, current evidence does not support the hypothesis that large portions of the genome are influenced by variations and that gene-specific selection drives the HapMap I LD scores, as suggested.

This study identifies and classifies 2-designs that satisfy specific conditions and have specific automorphism properties. A non-trivial 2-design's automorphism group can either be an instance of the previously documented examples described in this research or a specific subgroup within a larger group of automorphisms that corresponds to a geometric linear transformation involving a prime number.

This study examines electronic correlation within confined hydrogen, helium and lithium ions in their base states using entropy measures. Different wavefunctions are used to better account for inter-electronic interactions. The resulting entropy values show sensitivity to these interactions. In situations of extremely tight confinement, Coulomb effects are minimized and models treating particles as independent or non-interacting pairs in an impenetrable sphere are increasingly applicable. Energy estimates derived from these models align well with existing literature values.

The velocity distribution of wide binary stars at large separations provides a unique opportunity to test gravitational laws at extremely low acceleration found in the outskirts of galaxies. This is particularly significant because existing theories of gravity, including modified gravity and dark matter models, often struggle to explain observed galactic rotation curves. Recent analyses focused on gravitational velocity anomalies in wide binaries, however, were hindered by limited and inaccurate data on these systems. This data issue, however, is now resolved thanks to high-precision astrometric data collected by the Gaia mission, enabling the creation of more comprehensive samples of wide binaries. This study utilizes such data to examine the velocity distributions of thousands of wide binaries to search for any potential velocity anomalies, ultimately laying the groundwork for more precise future investigations to test gravitational laws at low acceleration environments.

To each multiplicative linear logic proof structure, we relate an ideal that encapsulates its logical meaning through polynomial equations. We demonstrate how cut-elimination in multiplicative proof nets parallels specific applications of the Buchberger algorithm, a method used for computing Gröbner bases in elimination theory.

A novel statistical method called cross-recurrence plot analysis is introduced to explore non-linear relationships and synchronized patterns between two time series variables, with applications demonstrated using financial data. Cross-recurrence quantification analysis serves as an extension to further examine patterns within cross-recurrence plots. This approach is distinguished by its capacity for simultaneous detection of non-linear connections and temporal relationships between variables, thereby addressing a gap in existing methods that only analyze one variable at a time or examine patterns in cross-sectional data. Cross-recurrence plot analysis is differentiated from related techniques such as joint recurrence plot analysis and cross-correlation analysis. Its computational efficiency and ease of interpretation are enhanced through automated and rapid methods for calculating cross-recurrence structure functions and visualizing cross-sectional time series relationships, leveraging three-dimensional visualizations and heat maps.

THz radiation enables the precise manipulation of confined electrons and holes,
inducing complex dynamics influenced by the zone radius, electric field intensity,
and radiation phase, leading to significant inertial effects from the circular motion of
these particles. Building upon recent research, this study investigates the impact of
both inertial and diamagnetic forces on a two-dimensional system containing
confining Coulomb interactions under the presence of a Coulomb barrier and a
resonant wave, with field intensity, radius, and phase all phase-controlled.
Simulations demonstrate that a combination of these two forces results in a diamagnetic
effect that counteracts the particle's motion, whereas the phase of the radiation leads to
a phase-locked circular motion, producing a balance between the two types of forces.
Additionally, this study reveals a radiative pressure that arises and can be tuned,
manifesting as the circular motion of the particles, similar to the radiation pressure
observed in atoms, where the particle's motion is driven by the balance of two radiation
forces in opposite directions.

Current click-through rate (CTR) prediction models are largely dependent on behavior logs, but their effectiveness is severely limited when applied to new, unseen advertisements lacking historical data. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a behavior-less side knowledge extraction framework, which harnesses external knowledge sources to enhance CTR predictions by incorporating ads' side content. Through the use of instance-level and attention mechanisms, we evaluate various attention models to select the optimal one, outperforming baseline models and significantly improving CTR predictions for novel ads with varying degrees of historical data. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed framework in addressing the cold-start problem in CTR prediction.

Business processes heavily reliant on human judgment and experience are frequently employed when dealing with uncertain or incomplete information, or when semi-structured processes need to be formalized, often resulting in business process models that omit essential information. Businesses also occasionally modify their processes for various reasons, leading to a need to fill in the gaps in the process description. Building on existing extensions to business process models like BPEL and YAWL, this research aims to develop a method for learning probabilistic business processes from observed examples, even when the process model contains unknown elements. To achieve this, a probabilistic variant of a petri net extension called CP-Nets is proposed, enabling CP-Nets to be learned probabilistically from observed processes, with a focus on learning both the process structure and the probabilities associated with it.

Wildfires have the potential to significantly impact solar energy generation through the reduction of solar irradiance, although specific fine-tuning of their effects remains a challenge. Moderate to severe forest fires can create non-condensable atmospheric aerosols known as ash, which is temporarily deposited on solar panels and simultaneously suspended in the atmosphere, thereby affecting their efficiency. We investigated the individual and combined effects of atmospheric ash and panel ash on solar energy production using a modified version of PySolar, a wildfire impact assessment tool. Our findings revealed that both atmospheric ash and panel ash need to be considered in order to accurately estimate the impact of wildfires on solar energy generation. We observed that panel ash has a more pronounced effect on solar energy output compared to atmospheric ash. We estimated that ash accumulation in the atmosphere could lower a solar panel's energy output by up to 14%, while dirty panels due to ash deposition could have energy outputs as low as 67%. We concluded that the temporary loss of solar energy productivity caused by ash deposition on panels is generally greater than the loss caused by atmospheric ash.

Protecting users of location-based services with significant privacy requirements is extremely difficult when multiple locations are shared within a short time frame due to the significant relationships anticipated between these locations. Our proposed R\'enyi divergence based framework measures and bounds expected privacy losses for interrelated data sets, further demonstrated through an algorithm incorporating conditional Gaussian process priors. This framework illustrates the challenges in safeguarding dependent data and provides a strategic approach to maintaining sensitive location data privacy within a specified boundary.

Research examining the brain's functional network during rest using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) typically analyzes regional networks from individual subjects, making it impossible to reduce this data without losing vital information. This requires researchers to utilize statistical methods that can handle complex data structures without assuming independence and equicorrelation, which are crucial considerations for multisite studies. A power investigation was conducted to assess whether common resting-state fMRI analysis methods can effectively detect differences and identify sites that vary systematically, taking into account individual differences and site variations. The results showed that standard two-sample and hotelling's t^2 tests have limited power in multisite studies, but a modified hotelling's t^2 test demonstrated the ability to identify differences and site variations, making it suitable for this type of research.

Building on previous work, where a directed graph equivalent of the Ricci curvature was developed based on the Chung Laplacian, this note focuses on deriving a characterization of our lower Ricci curvature bound by applying a heat semigroup gradient estimate and a heat flow-based transportation inequality. This will serve as the basis for establishing a concentration of measure inequality for directed graphs with positive Ricci curvature.

Recent advances in NLP for code-mixed texts have gained considerable attention, 
primely due to the rising popularity of social media across global communities. 
This work embeds word embeddings into a multilingual embedding space encompassing 
Hindi and English, which are crucial for effectively addressing code-switching 
phenomena. Our approach incorporates switchable segments of text into the 
embedding process. This is accomplished by considering both language tokens and 
domain-specific tokens such as punctuation and domains. These domains include 
domains from Twitter and Wikipedia. This strategy facilitates seamless 
integration of switchable tokens and their associated texts within a unified 
vector embedding space. This work evaluates the effectiveness of these domains 
on NLP tasks including word similarity, one-word translation, and question 
answering. The domain-based approach exhibits a notable $6.1\%$ enhancement 
over the non-domain-based method on the QA task.

Using a functional gradient method to model the electron-phonon interaction within hexasulfur at high pressures, we simulate how the electron-phonon coupling and $T_{c}$ change as a function of pressure in H$_3$S. Our model accurately replicates previous simulation and experimental findings on the electron-phonon coupling, $T_{c}$, and isotope effect, particularly in H$_3$S between 150 GPa and 230 GPa. Applying our method to investigate the H$_3$S electron structure, we find that an increase in energy sensitivity in the density of states contributes to the rise in $T_{c}$ within this pressure range. Additionally, we use our electron structure to study $T_{c}$ in bi- and tritium isotopes and observe an electron mass renormalization lower than anticipated, suggesting that H$_3$S may serve as a model for superconducting hydrides with intermediate to high $T_{c}$.

Fadmen Teicher and Aron D. Korajczyk developed a novel statistical approach for analyzing high-dimensional, dependent categorical data, building on dependent q-curve regression first introduced by Teicher and Wu in their 2019 work. This statistical tool is uniquely suited for revealing causation rather than mere correlation. In this paper, we showcase the efficacy of the approach in high-dimensional settings through its application to the analysis of twin data from a study on common adult-onset intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, previously reported by Chen et al. in Cell Research in 2020. By employing correlation and covariance calculations, the method identifies spurious associations, clustering, and causative patterns within large datasets. Ultimately, this approach serves as an extension of popular dimensionality reduction techniques such as PCA, FCCA, and FDC, enabling researchers to extract meaningful patterns from complex data while retaining the focus on causal relationships.

This paper will present our approach to developing a realistic walking robot, 
the RoboClown, utilizing advanced control systems and unconventional power 
sources like thrusters to bring about innovative movements. By integrating 
thrusters into the toes, knuckles, and fingers, we've achieved a highly 
customizable joint torque distribution, allowing us to utilize these technologies 
to create unique walking styles such as slow, precise strides. Additionally, the 
precise placement of foot sensors within the toes enables a natural forward 
extension during the walking cycle. Moreover, the presence of fingers contributes 
to maintaining balance and facilitates a more streamlined walking motion. 

Furthermore, we've integrated the robot with a virtual environment through the 
use of the Simulation System Interface (SSI), an open standard that facilitates 
communication with physical robots via the KRL language. Leveraging this 
connection, we've developed a straightforward method to simulate and simulate 
various stepping patterns, providing a practical tool for analyzing and 
enhancing physical stepping performance.

This research proposes a visual relocalization technique based on geometric information derived from 3D surfel mapping. A comprehensive database of images is initially created, incorporating 3D geometric details derived from corresponding visual data, obtained through multi-view stereo or pre-existing formats. A robust surfel map is constructed by aggregating detailed geometric information across diverse view perspectives. A single image is then utilized to accurately and precisely locate the view based on optimal geometric alignment with the established database. Furthermore, this method can accurately and efficiently determine view orientation. Notably, using a comprehensive view-based database and determining orientation yields superior performance in visual relocalization compared to utilizing partial geometric information from 2D and 2.5D formats.

Recent research in federated learning has highlighted the significance of client data heterogeneity, which often results in partial labels and data shifts. Current approaches that mitigate these drawbacks mainly rely on pre-trained models, which are unrealistic for a fully labeled target domain. Consequently, there is a pressing need for solutions that address label scarcity and data shifts in the field of federated learning. This study introduces a novel framework, referred to as FL2S, that tackles partial labeling and domain shifts through local adaptation and a loss function that adapively shifts. The FL2S framework empowers each participant to utilize unlabeled data and avoids fixed constraints on the shift type. By collaborating with other participants with diverse data, participants can improve the model and the overall performance. Results from extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed framework and show substantial performance gains over existing baselines.

Following a black hole-neutron star merger, a massive accretion disk forms around the black hole, and accretion onto this disk is believed to harbor potential for powering various astrophysical phenomena, such as short gamma-ray bursts and gravitational waves.  Numerical simulations of black hole-neutron star mergers have yielded a detailed understanding of how accretion disks form, yet the complex dynamics of this accretion process remain unclear.  A detailed analysis of an accretion disk resulting from such a merger reveals the following:  a substantial disk, comprising approximately 0.006 solar masses, develops within a few milliseconds, and a quasi-steady state is achieved within 100 milliseconds.  Following a brief transient phase, four relatively stable accretion episodes occur, each corresponding to a distinct relaxation process within the disk, and characterized by distinct timescales of approximately 100 milliseconds, 300 milliseconds, 1000 milliseconds, and 5000 milliseconds.  Ejections of magnetic flux from the disk trigger turbulent instabilities, which in turn initiate three types of accretion variability, corresponding to the accretion accretion episodes, and accurately modeled by distinct physical processes, including a Lense-Thirring precession, a magnetorotational instability, and a global magnetic dynamo, respectively.  A comparison of these processes reveals that, while magnetic processes play a crucial role in the accretion

A novel variation of the Kawazumi-Zhang invariant, specifically $\varphi(C)$,
for compact Riemann surfaces $C$ of genus $g \geq 1$ is presented, exploring
its connections to the first Mumford-Morita-Miller class $e_1 = \kappa_1$ on the
moduli space and its relation to the traditional Kawazumi-Zhang invariant.

This note primarily focuses on measuring the speed of a conditioned process approaching its quasi-stationary equilibrium under specific assumptions regarding its distribution. In reverse, we establish that a conditioned process converging uniformly to a self-conservative, ergodic Markov process also attains a distinct quasi-stationary equilibrium, which it converges toward at an exponential rate across all initial distributions. Furthermore, we illustrate a corollary ergodic theorem under specific conditions.

This research explores the optical interaction between a dimer of dielectric nanoparticles near a graphene layer. By applying a precise electromagnetic model, we computed the optical force acting on each particle and derived equations to assess the influence of graphene's surface plasmons. Our findings demonstrate that the excitation of graphene's surface plasmons can produce numerous stable positions with interparticle distances much shorter than the photon wavelength. Additionally, we found that these positions can be dynamically manipulated by adjusting the graphene's chemical potential. Both perpendicular and angled light incidence have been taken into account in our study.

A common issue in emergency departments (EDs) across the United States is the prolonged admission delay for abdominal pain patients. The objective of this study was to determine if increasing Emergency Department treatment duration can reduce the number of patients admitted and improve their subsequent hospital course. The analysis included more than 11,000 patients who received a treatment extension in an ED between 2015 and 2017. By comparing patients treated for 4-5 hours with those treated for 5-6 hours, the study found that extending treatment time was associated with a significant decrease in hospital admission rates (4 percentage point reduction, or 11% decrease) and similar rates of return to the ED or hospital admission within 30 days. The proposed mechanism for these positive outcomes involves increased emergency physician observation time and improved communication with hospital physicians, which benefits not only patients but also emergency departments by decreasing future admissions and improving operational efficiency.

In cooperative systems with multiple agents, we investigate task completion under various settings of limited and shared information. We consider a group of agents with varying levels of cognitive abilities, where each agent has access to either shared or individual data sources. To ensure reliable task completion, we define a standard of reliability based on executing optimal strategies in scenarios with no information sharing, leading to a Nash equilibrium outcome. Our study focuses on two types of tasks: finding a group of items that meet certain criteria and making a series of decisions among group options. We develop efficient algorithms for these tasks and provide performance guarantees in the form of utility approximations near Nash equilibrium solutions.

Research has been conducted to investigate correlations caused by the Chiral Magnetic Effect (CME) in heavy-ion collisions, by examining sub-entropy-cone correlations of various particle pairs relative to the event plane and their association with charged-particle multiplicity. These correlations were investigated in proton-proton and proton-lead collisions to investigate potential influences from other phenomena, such as those arising from charge separation within large charge clusters. A method was developed to isolate correlations arising from CME and other global effects by using events with minimum bias and events with the lowest and highest event-plane angles as reference points. This approach enabled the isolation of correlations due to global effects in heavy-ion collisions, while suggesting that particle pairs with perpendicular charge relative to the event-plane exhibit the distinct characteristics of the Chiral Magnetic Effect.

The surge in online crowdfunding platforms has transformed the landscape of funding for creative projects, allowing individuals and groups to pursue their ideas with a broader base of potential supporters. As thousands of projects are launched on these sites, understanding the factors driving their financial success has become imperative. Existing studies have sought to explore this, but their limitations in providing actionable insights for project creators and funders remain. This study addresses this gap by examining how funders' behavioral cues influence crowdcreated's success, utilizing nearly 70,000 signals collected through surveys and reviews from crowdcreators, along with project details and outcome data. Through advanced data analysis techniques, our results reveal that signals such as active engagement and positive feedback significantly increase a project's likelihood of reaching its funding goal, highlighting the importance of engaging with funders and responding to their input. These findings highlight opportunities for funders and project creators to foster meaningful connections and sustained fundership relationships.

Machine learning (ML) based detection of network attacks using ML frameworks has become a prevalent approach, but it presents several challenges, primarily stemming from the need to integrate diverse data sets, such as public and private data, and advanced ML models, for which specialized tools and expertise are essential. This research addresses these issues by introducing an open-source Python package, called MLPD, that simplifies the process of developing custom ML-based intrusion detection systems, even for those with limited knowledge of machine learning and data science. Our package enables easy intrusion data loading, preprocessing, and conversion of various ML models, as well as the comparison of their effectiveness in different intrusion detection scenarios. Additionally, the design of our system allows for the evaluation of model performance under multiple intrusion detection strategies, thus facilitating model selection and validation. Through comprehensive experiments, we validate the efficiency of our package and demonstrate its ability to model different intrusion detection strategies, thereby enabling reusability and adaptability to novel attack types. Our code and documentation are available at https://github.com/hasan-khokhar/MLPD.

This research addresses the issue of real-time task scheduling for a robot, where the task list is generated instantly by a controller. The objective is to determine the most efficient sequence of tasks that minimizes overall execution time, yet remains feasible by ensuring each task can be completed within a specified time frame. The challenge is compounded by the fact that some tasks require the robot to move between different locations, introducing movement constraints and preventing optimization through standard dynamic programming methods, which rely on the optimal substructure property. The task and movement interdependence also rules out the application of a two-stage method, typically used in planning and control systems. The proposed solution introduces a task classification method, dividing tasks into groups that can be executed simultaneously, and adapts the classic Wright rule algorithm for optimal scheduling, which is efficient at handling various types of constraints and does not depend on dynamic programming properties. The solution efficiently handles complex tasks, such as those involving multiple robot arms, visual constraints, and camera adjustments, and has been validated through numerical examples that demonstrate its applicability even in scenarios with limited look-ahead planning.

The performance of the interface between semiconductors and barriers is a crucial factor in producing consistent, high-quality quantum dots essential for reliable quantum information processing. This research investigates the characteristics of undoped Si substrates by measuring SiMOSFET Hall bars, thereby evaluating the quality of fully fabricated CMOS devices. A notable mobility level of 18,500 cm^2/Vs was achieved with oxide thickness below 10 nm, showcasing a superior interface ideal for use in qubit-based technologies. Additionally, the study explores the impact of different gate materials on mobility and identifies the underlying principles to guide future optimizations of quantum computing hardware.

In complex networks, a phenomenon occurs where different clusters of oscillators, comprised of distinct types, synchronize with their own distinct rhythms. We investigate this complex synchronization dynamics in systems of coupled oscillators, using a generalized Hopfield model that includes multiple frequencies and includes both long-range and short-range interactions. The system allows for both homogeneous and inhomogeneous dynamics in space. Our study reveals that, in systems with short-range interactions only, synchronization becomes impossible across different spatial regions. However, when long-range interactions are present, we observe that clusters of oscillators can synchronize within their own distinct rhythms, even if they are not aligned with others. Furthermore, our research demonstrates that synchronized patterns can emerge spontaneously, even in random systems, and that these patterns can be influenced by the system's connectivity and the presence of heterogeneity.

Our research examines the existence of domain-specific search engines for western languages by comparing the search outcomes of English, German, and Dutch queries across three major search engines, focusing on video results. The evaluation measures result diversity in terms of video sources, relevance, and semantic meaning. Our findings suggest that most video sources prioritize non-western languages, and translating queries to the languages of these sources significantly boosts relevance and improves semantic similarity. Notably, these benefits are more pronounced in smaller search engines, and our data indicates that translating queries can effectively enhance the relevance of search results without necessitating the development of specialized multilingual search engines for specific domains.

To gain insight into supersymmetric monodromy defects in the critical Wess-Zumino model, researchers employed analytical bootstrap techniques, providing a detailed examination of their correlation functions. The techniques involved splitting the complex plane into distinct regions separated by supersymmetric monodromy defects and expressing each region's correlation function expansion in terms of its adjacent region. This was achieved by applying conformal partial waves that respect the supersymmetric monodromy's representation theory. Additionally, by enforcing invariance across the supersymmetric monodromy defects, a system of equations was derived, allowing for the determination of coupling constants. The results were supplemented with numerical bootstrap bounds to establish inequalities for coupling constants, ultimately leading to the precise computation of supersymmetric monodromy defects' correlation functions. Furthermore, researchers derived a factorization property for supersymmetric monodromy defects, validating their factorization into simpler conformal blocks.

We prove that there is exactly one elliptic curve, up to uniqueness, defined over a cubic Galois field extension of rational numbers with a point on the curve having an order of 13 that is rational in the extension and that curve is not defined by the rational numbers.

The capacity of wireless networks is inherently influenced by interference, and while interference correlation has been acknowledged, its connection to spatially diverse local delays remains understudied. Through analytical and numerical evaluation, we establish a direct inverse proportionality between the number of Hertz and the average local time delay in wireless networks, providing a proportionality constant that scales logarithmically with the number of devices. By examining the spectrum of a wireless network, we can derive a precise and scalable formula for the logarithmic constant, and investigate the influence of interference, channel parameters, and spectrum allocation on network time delay. These findings yield a novel design principle for wireless networks, where the interference correlation matrix is represented by a linear combination of a deterministic matrix and a logarithmic function of the frequency, specifically tailored to narrowband environments.

A pseudo-labeling framework is proposed to address the problem of abundant unlabeled yet sparsely labeled data, a common challenge when training Graph Neural Network (GNN) models. Existing methods that utilize unlabeled data for pseudo-labeling generate multiple candidate labels and employ a consistency loss based on GNN outputs with various or multiple input perturbations. This approach has two main drawbacks: the reliance on a pre-trained GNN model and the stability of the consistency loss. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents a new pseudo-labeling method that generates a single, high-quality pseudo-label for each node by leveraging node centrality as a reliable indicator and creating a cluster-specific target distribution to guide the GNN model's output. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, which is named CentNode, in pan-optical image change detection and semi-supervised node classification tasks.

This research introduces a novel training framework called PatchLearn for video classification, featuring a innovative patchwise feature learning approach. Unlike conventional pixel feature learning, our method divides videos into spatial patches to capture global semantic information and optimize computation. Furthermore, we develop a new evaluation metric, PatchNMF, to quantify the quality of learned features by embedding patches into 2D manifolds. Extensive evaluations across various architectures and video datasets demonstrate the superiority of PatchLearn, achieving record-breaking performance of up to 76.2% in top-1 accuracy for Kinetics-400 with a computational cost 2.4X cheaper than the existing state-of-the-art.

We examine the one-dimensional discrete-time asymmetric exclusion process with periodic boundaries, using parallel updates and a generalizable method for obtaining the transition matrix. A specific choice of Lukovics' update rules allows for detailed analysis, leading to new insights into the eigenvalues and a complete understanding of the time-evolution operator through a known basis and nontrivial R-matrix integration technique.

A new method is proposed to enhance the energy and data efficiency of a specific type of mobile data network that uses wireless energy transfer from a multi-antenna base station to multiple single-antenna energy-harvesting users who then share their data through a type of wireless communication called backhaul link. A specific type of wireless communication protocol, known as the decode-and-forward scheme, is used to maximize the data flow between user groups in this network. A specific type of energy transfer protocol, simultaneous wireless information and power transfer, is used to allow the energy-harvesting users to collect both energy and power simultaneously. A specific algorithm is developed to determine the best power allocation and data transmission strategies that will maximize the total data flow while adhering to various constraints such as total power consumption, power usage limits for a specific type of energy communication protocol, and a type of energy harvesting energy harvesting. This algorithm uses a type of mathematical optimization and an algorithm that breaks a complex problem into a simpler one, and it converges rapidly with accurate solutions found within a small margin of error. Simulation results confirm the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed algorithm and highlight its ability to adapt to different system parameters.

In Fermi gases with low density, the transition from spin-balanced to spin-imbalanced states is a second-order event, characterized by a change in the type of excitation from sound waves to Goldstone modes as seen in a Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer state. Using the variational method, this research determines how certain parameters, such as energy and energy levels, evolve through the transition point for spin systems of three or more types. The findings confirm the continuous, second-order nature of the phase change, with results matching those from more complex BCS theory predictions made in the thermodynamic sense. Furthermore, by making additional assumptions, this variational method can be applied to model how the parameters of thermal energies and response rates change at high temperatures within thermodynamic models.

We present a generic and easy-to-use model for electric circuit analysis, which is applicable to various types of electro- and optomechanical systems. The model, based on a parallel RLC circuit, reveals that a mechanical oscillator functions as a moving plate capacitor whose area changes due to mechanical displacement. By applying a Hermitian system approach, we take into account the back-action forces induced by quantum electromagnetic fields on both the electrical and mechanical components, which is equivalent to the back-action amplitude force commonly used in optomechanical models. Furthermore, our model can be seamlessly integrated with other components, such as an optical cavity, to develop novel optomechanical systems with customizable RLC structures.

Semi-classical orthogonal polynomials generalising the Racah polynomials can be defined using a generalized Airy weight, which depends on two parameters, subject to specific constraints. The generalized form includes an exponent parameter that must be a non-negative integer subject to an upper constraint. Closed-form expressions for the moment integrals and the recurrence coefficients in the three-term recurrence relation have been derived, along with the explicit form of the polynomials obtained through a method based on hypergeometric series, previously established by Mokhov. The parameter for the generalized Airy weight can be extended to real values, although this extension is limited under certain conditions. The polynomial form can also be expressed as a sum of two hypergeometric functions, revealing a connection with the Racah polynomials, specifically showing that these semi-classical polynomials reduce to classical Racah polynomials under specific parameter values.

This study investigates how basic autonomous entities behave in a basic cellular automaton with a non-uniform energy distribution. These entities move along a horizontal surface and draw their energy from its immediate surroundings. We demonstrate that these autonomous entities can exhibit complex movement patterns, such as traveling in straight lines or moving in a circular path, depending on their nearby energy supply. We simulate their movement using a Markov chain and calculate properties like the duration and frequency of their movement. When their movement follows a circular pattern, the frequency is found to decrease as the parameter representing disordered movement increases.

This article further explores and develops the concept of chiral aspects in 2-dimensional spacetimes within quantum field theory, focusing on locally non-anticipative states. Building upon established foundations, we establish a precise framework for quantizing the classical canonical commutation relations, thereby enabling an efficient and intuitive approach to defining quasi-free states. Various types of quasi-free states are examined, with particular emphasis on algebras derived from past light cones in globally hyperbolic spacetimes. These specific states allow us to derive a simplified, yet comprehensive set of operator equations, providing a straightforward method for computing two-point functions.

Laparoscopic surgery employs a laparoscope to provide real-time visual guidance for surgeons operating through small incisions, but the laparoscope's illumination can cause the surgery site to appear overly bright, making it difficult to visualize tissue details, especially with inexperienced surgeons. Incidentally, this brightness also obscures smoke generated during the procedure to protect surgeons' vision and the patient's lungs. An innovative technique has been developed to clarify the visualization of tissues and remove smoke through a two-step process, utilizing an advanced deep learning approach, especially valuable for surgeons performing proctology surgeries laparoscopically.

This research focuses on creating resilient Molmer-Sorensen gates using trapped ions arranged in a line, incorporating Gaussian amplitude modulation and a consistent laser frequency to improve their resistance to frequency errors. We chose a frequency tuning method that简ifies implementation while maintaining efficiency, and our computational analysis demonstrates the benefits of this approach, particularly in situations with limited spectral range. Moreover, we discovered a specific trajectory in the spectral domain that yields an optimal, parameter-free gate when a certain condition is met between the spheroidal harmonic frequency and the dipole transition spread, even for diatomic systems. We also outline a straightforward method for detecting and correcting time-dependent frequency shifts using a specialized modulation trajectory, thus ensuring robustness without prior frequency detection. We believe this research has significant practical value for experimental applications, particularly for systems with simple spectra but complex energy level structures, such as $^{171}$Yb$^{+}$ and $^{131}$Ba$^{+}$, for which we provide numerical illustrations and assess the impact of motion on gate reliability.

Using advanced particle swarm optimization in combination with a robust global optimization method, we generate large populations of potential structures for barium titanium oxide and perform extensive density functional theory calculations to evaluate their stability. This extensive search allows us to identify previously unknown prototypes that exhibit a high degree of structural similarity to the original material. Our findings reveal that 26 out of 27 prototypes are stable in their respective phases, with 19 being paraelectric and 7 being ferroelectric. Moreover, our paraelectric prototypes show excellent agreement with experimental data, featuring a $T_C$ temperature range of 235-245 K, which closely matches real-world observations.

Multivariate functional time series analysis typically relies on covariance functions, which are notoriously difficult to interpret. In contrast, counting the score counts between time series components can provide clearer insights, but this becomes impractical for complex data sets due to the enormous number of counts involved. We introduce a new class of graphical models tailored for multivariate functional data, focusing on scalar observations from individual time series components and representing inter-component relationships through precision matrices. By dimensionally reducing covariance functions to finitely many scores, we make feasible the estimation of cross-component dependencies and obtain a interpretable structure. Our approach accommodates various scalar observations formats, from discrete counts to continuous values, and can be applied to individual scores or a combination of scores. Consequently, some scores may be conditionally dependent on others but not directly connected, and this dependence structure can be captured in a single estimated pairwise relationship. Our method is demonstrated on two examples and its performance evaluated on two simulated data sets, ultimately allowing for a clear and intuitive interpretation of functional network structures.

Existing quantum processors are prone to errors and have limited lifespan due to
imperfect gate operations and noise. To run algorithms successfully, they must
be completed within their coherence times. Variational quantum algorithms, such as
the quantum variational eigensolver, can tolerate some errors and do not require
large numbers of repetitions. Their lack of complex multi-controlled gates makes
them a promising approach for computations on small-scale quantum devices. In this
study, we introduce a quantum algorithm designed to find the lowest eigenvalue and
associated wave function of a target Hamiltonian, completing it in a reasonable
amount of time even with current noisy quantum processors. We also evaluate its
performance using Qiskisb for various quantum circuits.

A recent approach to optimizing techniques employs average-case analysis, 
evaluating performance based on characteristics of a problem's underlying matrix. 
Achieving convergence rates close to the matrix's extremal eigenvalues necessitates 
iterative procedures with an expected number of steps linked to the matrix's eigenvalue 
distribution at those boundaries. We investigate this matter from a different angle, 
analyzing optimization's expected complexity in relation to various random matrix models, 
including those involving spiked matrices, regardless of their size or convergence to a limiting distribution. Our analysis reveals that for certain instances, such as small "signal" sizes or extremely low noise levels, we can bypass rates tied to the main body of the spectral distribution, as the relevant eigenvalues are concentrated at the spectrum's edges. This approach has demonstrated that many problems can be solved in linear time, yet it also shows, for example, in signal detection scenarios, that average-case performance can vary significantly based on whether the problem is theoretically solvable.

Recent breakthroughs in producing two-dimensional materials with specific patterns of layered structures have paved the way for novel inventions in optoelectronics and quantum information technology. Within this type of structure, a novel particle called an exciton-polaron has been identified, composed of four constituent parts arranged in two layers. The excitation in one layer interacts with the excitations within its adjacent layers to form a bound state, driven by the interplay between their electrical and magnetic fields. The layers are connected through long-range Coulomb interactions, which give rise to the formation of this exciton-polaron state. The two-particle state formed from these interacting inter- and intralayer excitons was initially considered unfeasible, due to the short lifespan of the involved particles. However, advancements in experimental techniques have enabled researchers to observe the formation of a biexciton composed of these two interacting components. The resulting bound state exhibits a notable energy level below zero, indicating a greater stability than separate states. The energy gap between the ground and first excited states allows for straightforward identification through spectroscopic analysis.

We have developed a method for determining the position of objects that accounts for various multipath effects, which are prevalent in areas with numerous obstacles like indoors and urban spaces. Our technique utilizes data from wireless communications systems that track signals at the receiver and accounts for the different paths signals take by analyzing their characteristics, such as direction and delay. By applying a technique known as ray tracing and using an optimization method that minimization a specific function, we can achieve more accurate positioning in these areas. Our approach has been thoroughly tested using simulated data and compared with existing methods that don't take multipath effects into consideration. Results show that the multipath-aware method outperforms the basic positioning method that ignores these effects in terms of accuracy and consistency.

Researchers have achieved the first observation of two vector bosons being produced and behaving like particles with spin in line with the direction of movement, for particles other than photons and Z bosons. This event, involving two completely spin-locked W bosons, was detected using a massive collection of data collected by the ATLAS detector at CERN's Large Hadron Collider, totaling 140 inverse femtobarns. The probability that this event occurred naturally, without influence from spin-locked vector bosons, was calculated to be less than one in 3.6 million, based on specific patterns left by bosons leaving decay products, and also through another measure, totaling one in 22,000. These findings demonstrate a significant level of confidence in boson coupling strength, at around 5.3 standard deviations, and provides a demonstration of selecting completely spin-locked events, providing a new tool to study these interactions in detail.

Research indicates that the Cotton tensor offers an alternative, single equation that can explain gravity and lead to a solution equivalent to Einstein's theory. A new, linearized gravity approach is presented in the article, which is based on the Cotton tensor. This method is supported by two key findings: first, that any metric's Cotton tensor can be expressed as a combination of the Cotton derivative operator and its adjoint, called the Schouten Laplacian, applied to the Schouten tensor; second, that Schouten Laplacians correspond to specific elliptic operators for various dimensions, with one exceptional case in seven dimensions. These operators' eigenfunctions represent gravitational waves, which are fully characterized by their eigenvalues and eigenmodes, providing a comprehensive set of representations for any given gravity field.

We've developed a specific type of ordered relational topological space called an orthomodular space. This concept unifies various existing ordered relational space types under one framework. Our work establishes a dual relationship between orthomodular spaces and a broad class of algebraic structures known as orthomodular algebras. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the collection of orthomodular spaces forms a comprehensive lattice structure under the Hausdorff convergence convergence, providing a unified generalization of the existing methods for constructing orthomodular algebraic structures.

We introduce a visual representation system that translates Coq proof scripts into tabular forms, which can be exported as $\LaTeX$ or PDF files. Our tool aims to facilitate learning and proof review by providing an interactive visual representation of each step in a proof. Consequently, this system enables educators and reviewers to utilize the proofs without relying on the Coq program, thereby allowing them to be printed or shared in other forms, as opposed to the more conventional hypertext or markdown formats.

We demonstrate that the fourth moment of holomorphic Hecke cusp forms is limited under the assumption of the Riemann Hypothesis for a specific degree 8 L-function. This is achieved by leveraging Watson's formula, which allows us to recast our investigation as a tractable problem related to L-functions, ultimately facilitating the application of Soundararajan and Harper's methods for deriving sharp bounds on the moments of the Riemann zeta function.

In interior point methods for optimizing convex problems, we address a system of linear equations at each iteration. To enhance efficiency, we develop faster direct solution methods or more convergent iterative methods by developing preconditioners that mirror the interior point algorithm's structure, thereby achieving optimal performance or convergence rates. These approaches yield preconditioned systems with improved properties, allowing solutions to be found more quickly using established methods, such as truncated Newton iterations, yielding near-exactly solved systems after just one or a few steps.

We have derived the polarized massive operator matrix element $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$
analytically to three-loop order in QCD for arbitrary values of $N$,
including both single- and double-mass scenarios in the Larin scheme.
Furthermore, the result serves as a crucial transition function for the variable
flavor number scheme at $O(\alpha_s^3)$ and is also expressed in momentum
space for convenient use.

Established industries such as aviation gather real-user feedback on problems with smart technologies through documented cases of system failure, injury, or close calls. A large database of such reported incidents, containing detailed descriptions of specific events and their contexts, can be used to identify common patterns of failure through advanced analysis methods. This research proposes an innovative approach that combines knowledge graph creation with pattern discovery to automatically extract meaningful patterns of failure from text-based reports of real users. The proposed framework generates a knowledge graph by manually categorizing key components within reports, and then uses an clustering algorithm to identify patterns of failure that match human understanding. The efficacy of this approach was validated through experiments conducted on two distinct datasets, demonstrating its ability to capture patterns consistent with human judgment while avoiding the need for extensive manual feature engineering.

The principle underlying the renormalization group bears a strong analogy to gradient flow, especially in scalar field theory where the RG and gradient flows share a direct connection through the ERG formalism established by Wilson and Kogut. Building on this concept, we propose an ERG method for conventional QCD that involves coupling the standard gluon-quark fields with a nonlocal and squared-time-derivative containing drift term, drawing inspiration from a similar relationship in complex complex Langevin simulations. This ERG framework can be formulated as a path integral with both local and nonlocal contributions, specifically including an inverse propagator of the form $P^2 + A$, where $P$ is a squared time derivative operator and $A$ is a mass term representing the Wilson flow. Consequently, our ERG framework mimics the Wilson flow while incorporating a nonlocal term already present in lattice QCD, thereby avoiding the typical issues associated with inverse propagator structures that often arise in attempts to link gradient flows and renormalization groups.

Current clinical guidelines are based on individual disease entities, however,
the application of these guidelines is complicated by symptoms that can be caused
by multiple diseases. In an effort to support medical decision-making, a novel
language model has been developed to suggest the most likely applicable clinical
guidelines based on a given set of symptoms. This innovative model can also
detect and highlight symptoms that are unusual or unexpected, and has the added
capability of inferring and recommending additional symptoms that a patient might
be experiencing but are as yet unreported. By being trained on electronic health
records, this model has been shown to significantly outperform traditional
methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency for both tasks.

Quipper, a domain-specific language, enables the description of quantum circuits by embedding them in Haskell. Recently, its linear type system was enhanced to prevent side effects while allowing shared variable usage through mutable references. This paper explores integrating higher-order functions into linear parts of the code to improve code readability and modularity, developing a new subtyping system to ensure that function calls comply with linear type constraints without causing undefined behavior related to quantum measurements.

In this study, we investigate critical phenomena in two-dimensional percolation models by analyzing the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of percolation clusters near the critical point. After generating numerous clusters at the critical point, we focused on smaller subsets of these clusters to determine their largest and second-largest eigenvalues. Our analysis revealed that the largest eigenvalue follows a power-law distribution, implying that extreme eigenvalues significantly impact critical behavior. Moreover, we developed a novel approach to estimate the second-largest eigenvalue, which shows a distinct power-law behavior, offering potential insight into understanding universal properties of critical phenomena.

We suggest an alternative approach to understanding lock-step dynamics, based on
interacting atoms that exchange virtual photons, leading to entanglement build-up
at an exponential rate, consistent with established predictions from quantum electrodynamics in
free space. Additionally, our model reveals that large systems exhibit the most rapid
entanglement growth but exhibit shorter durations of entanglement due to the virtual photon's
shorter lifetime.

Assembling a complete genome from short, overlapping DNA sequences is a complex computational task, especially when genomes come from multiple individuals. To address this challenge, we've developed a novel approach called MultiFrac, specifically tailored for assembling genomes from multiple similar organisms. Building on the Frank-Soloveva assembler, which constructs graphs of genomes and identifies their shared and unique components, we've adapted this method to integrate genomes of multiple individuals. Our approach initially identifies the common structure of these genomes before introducing individual variations. By carefully introducing these differences, we extract the distinct genomes of each organism. We evaluated this method on synthetic DNA sequences and actual genomes of yeasts, and found that it enables accurate reconstruction of individual genomes with high resolution.

A classic delayed logistic equation, originally developed by Hutchinson in 1942 to address oscillations in ecological systems with time-lag, is revisited. This delayed differential equation lacks a conventional phase space, prompting an alternative approach to its analysis. By adapting a phase space framework and integrating novel technical strategies, we characterize the solution set's global behavior, ultimately proving the system exhibits all the ecological patterns observed in its nondelayed logistic counterpart.

The concept of statistical depth has the potential to be used in analyzing temporal patterns and making various measures of central tendency and order statistics available for such data. However, direct application of this concept is complicated by the requirement that depth be defined over a comprehensive data set. As a result, it is impractical for modeling temporal point processes where events may occur at any given time. The issue is addressed by developing methods for computing depth for temporal point processes using two approaches: one involves using a parameterized model to represent the expected distribution of events, while the other relies on the timing and frequency of events within a specified duration. The methods are evaluated through simulation studies, showing that they provide meaningful insights and parameter estimates for typical scenarios. Furthermore, they are applied to real-world data from the field of transcranial magnetic stimulation, where they are used to create individualized event profiles and estimate necessary stimulation parameters for achieving desired brain activation patterns.

Achieving maximum engine performance involves leveraging quantum effects. In this investigation, two strategies for creating the most efficient engines are considered, specifically (1) using hybrid quantum systems capable of performing tasks faster than any classical equivalent and (2) exploiting quantum systems with unique statistical properties to power these machines. In order to illustrate these concepts, a versatile model is presented in this study. It is based on a quantum tunneling particle interacting with a collective of harmonic oscillators representing a collective quantum bath and coupled to a massless oscillator representing the output load. By defining various scenarios for the quantum side massless oscillator configurations, distinct statistical characteristics can be established. It was discovered that hybrid quantum effects and distinct statistical properties can significantly improve engine speed and output speed, respectively. Additionally, optimal performance was maximized through careful tuning of key parameters such as tunneling and damping. Furthermore, performance was shown to be influenced by a key parameter mass ratio. These results provide valuable insights into quantum thermodynamics and offer avenues for further theoretical exploration and experimental validation.

Researchers investigated the nuclear characteristics of the isotopes $^{69}$Ge, $^{71}$Ge, and $^{73}$Ge using a precise set of measurements performed at the ISOLDE facility of CERN. By combining multiple measurement methods, researchers obtained significantly improved values for certain nuclear properties and discovered that certain assumptions about certain nuclear behaviors were not universally applicable. Specifically, researchers found that the magnetic and quadrupole moments of $^{69}$Ge deviated significantly from previously predicted values, whereas the octupole moments of $^{69}$Ge, $^{71}$Ge, and $^{73}$Ge aligned well with the predictions made by the Hartree-Fock-Meshbach model. Furthermore, researchers determined that the assumption of a uniform behavior in certain octupole moments in certain nuclear pairs was not applicable to certain triads of isotopes.

Researchers at the Research Center for Nuclear Physics in Bonn, Germany, have introduced a novel technique for precisely measuring the masses of brief-lived, unusual atomic nuclei. This is achieved by combining a highly sensitive atomic clock, specifically a $^{171}$Yb$^{+}$ ion clock, with an innovative production method for antiprotonic helium near its Bohr orbit. By cancelling out most environmental factors influencing atomic clocks, such as a trap-induced shift and an original experiment-induced frequency shift caused by antiproton influence, researchers were able to make precise adjustments and achieve a $^{166m}$Ho mass determination with exceptional accuracy, resulting in a breakthrough measurement with only 13 parts per billion uncertainty.

This tutorial outlines a Monte Carlo method used in lattice field theories that utilizes importance sampling to estimate properties of Boltzmann distributions. 
For a more hands-on experience, participants are encouraged to engage with the accompanying Jupyter notebook.

We aim to enhance the accuracy of structured text recognition by incorporating predefined formats defined through regular expressions, thereby facilitating the identification of specific patterns. Our method, involving a Weighted Finite-State Transducer model, boosts recognition accuracy on targeted formats, with minimal losses in other instances. A key parameter governs the intensity of the formatting influence. The proposed technique finds applications in text analysis, search engine optimization, and the definition of text-based contracts.

The CMS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider detected the production of long-lived particles that decay into muons as a result of prompt production processes, specifically muon + signed momentum sign reversal of di-muon systems, in data collected at 13 TeV with a total luminosity of 92 fb$^{-(-1)}$.  A novel search strategy that doesn't depend on detection efficiency was employed.  A significant signal above the expected background was identified in data, with a significance of 6.8 standard deviations.  This search covered a broad range of muon momentum, and particles were detected outside of existing exclusion limits set by other experiments.  The discovery threshold was set at 5 standard deviations.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed framework over baseline models in terms of execution and exact set match accuracy when database contents are inaccessible, with further analysis pointing to areas for future improvement.

A groundbreaking radio survey called LOFAR Two-Metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) is providing crucial data on the large-scale structure of the Universe by mapping intense, radio-emitting galaxies and groups. Based in the Netherlands, the LoTSS team is utilizing a 20-metre radio telescope to map the northern and southern skies with exceptional detail. Each square degree of the sky is monitored for 3.5 hours at frequencies near 150 MHz, revealing intense galaxies up to 10 millijanskys in various weaknesses. Initially, LoTSS will focus on mapping large galaxies, with future research exploring fainter galaxies in the distant Universe. Preliminary data from LoTSS will be utilized for studying the Universe's large-scale structure and utilizing galaxies as markers for 3D maps of the Universe's volume analyzed for 30 billion cubic megaparsecs.

The High-Dimensional Rank Lasso (HDR Lasso) model offers a computationally efficient solution to handle complex data analysis, specifically for high-dimensional regression tasks. However, the computational demands increase with the size of the dataset, which can be a bottleneck for modern, large-scale data. We introduce the High-Dimensional Simplex Lasso (HSD Lasso) method, a computationally efficient alternative to HDR Lasso, leveraging Conic Lasso solutions. By formulating an LVFRP problem and exploiting the properties of the simplex and spectral decomposition, HSD Lasso achieves significant speed improvements while maintaining robustness and model interpretability. Empirical results demonstrate the efficiency gains of HSD Lasso in the context of DNA sequencing data analysis.

Identifying whether an optimal solution is localized or universal is particularly challenging in complex optimization problems. This work addresses that challenge by demonstrating the existence of a single, optimal method for controlling thermodynamic systems at any given temperature to achieve maximum efficiency in the shortest time possible.
